name: Particle / VFX Lab
_note: Four systems, side by side on a black ground, and each one exists to make ONE of the compute pipeline's decisions readable on its own. The lab owns emission, simulation, compaction and the indirect draw (src/rendering/particle_renderer.cpp, shaders/particles.wgsl); it does not own the fields that push particles about, which are authored scene data and belong to the World Effects work. So: no field forces here, no wind, no attractors and no curl turbulence on the two systems the counting cases read. Every number this lab measures should be arithmetic over spawnRate, lifetime and capacity, and a fixture that stirred them with a noise field would make every reading a joint measurement of two subsystems. The four are: (1) 'metered', rate 3000/s and lifetime 0.5 s, so the pool settles at rate*lifetime = 1500 alive and a case can check the pool occupancy against a number written in this file; (2) 'saturated', the same rate into a capacity of 256, which cannot hold a lifetime's worth -- cs_emit clamps to the free slots and this is where that clamp is visible rather than inferred; (3) 'trailed', ADR-040 ribbons at stride 1, the one system whose per-frame write is keyed to the frame index rather than to the timeline second; (4) 'burst', spawnRate 0 with burst 64, so a case can separate the per-frame rate from the per-frame burst -- they are added in ParticleRenderer::update and nothing else in the repository distinguishes them. The camera is 26 m back with a 40 degree vertical field of view; the systems sit at x = -9, -3, 3, 9 so each occupies its own quarter of the frame and a case can measure one without windowing the others out. The ground is a single unlit black box rather than nothing, so the depth prepass has something to write and the soft-particle and fog-coupling arms have a surface to be occluded by. Nothing here authors post settings: a case sets those through the post/* parameters.
